statement: Use the H(4,3) coordinate order (004,013,022,031,040,103,112,121,130,202,211,220,301,310,400). For every gamma in BR_{\mathring Q}(4,3) intersect Z^{H(4,3)} satisfying gamma_103 <= 0, gamma_112 <= 0, gamma_301 <= 0, and gamma_alpha >= 0 at each of the other twelve coordinates, there exists C(gamma)>0 such that C(gamma)D_gamma-N_gamma is coefficientwise nonnegative in the twelve formal variables a_ri. This claim includes all boundary lattice points of that closed sign chamber and makes no assertion about integral cone points outside it; in particular it does not resolve the frozen universal conjecture.
contribution: An exact rank-12 saturated-lattice computation reconstructs this full-dimensional closed chamber from both V- and H-representations. PyNormaliz 2.24 returns the same complete 134-element Hilbert basis from both descriptions (48 extreme rays and 86 non-ray elements), every generator is directly checked against the balance, lattice, facet, and sign constraints, and every generator passes exact ordinary-coefficient support containment. Sign compatibility and Hilbert generation then prove the stated chamber theorem. This advances the source's ray-level evidence to every integral point of one complete chamber while preserving the unresolved status of the original problem.
